newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: BELGIAN PM DOES NOT SEE U.K. JOINING EMU IN 1999.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN PM DOES NOT SEE U.K. JOINING EMU IN 1999.

text.p: Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene said on Thursday he did not expect Britain to be among the first wave of European countries adopting the euro as their currency on January 1, 1999.

But Dehaene, whose bid two years ago for presidency of the European Commission was blocked by British Prime Minister John Major, said Britain would eventually bow to pressure from the City of London and join.

"I think the history of the European Union will repeat itself - that in 1998 Britain will decide it's not in its national interest to go into monetary union and then two or three years later decide it is," Dehaene said.

Dehaene was speaking to journalists after receiving the "Vision for Europe" prize from the Edmond Israel Foundation, named after former Luxembourg bourse chairman and founder of the Cedel clearing bank.
In a speech, Dehaene said he believed economic and monetary union (EMU) would take place according to the timetable set out in the EU's Maastricht Treaty.
The Treaty foresees EU leaders deciding before July 1998 on which countries are eligible to lock their exchange rates in a currency union from January 1, 1999.
